chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying, 'Singing is from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has promised the Fire for it,'

and he recited this Verse: 'And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to lead astray from the way of Allah without knowledge and to take it in mockery. Those will have a humiliating punishment.'

key_terms.الْغِنَاءُ: Singing or vocal music, specifically in a musical context
key_terms.لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ: Amusing discourse or diverting speech, often interpreted as singing

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on singing (ghina') based on the hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies al-ghina' (singing) as a specific cause for Hellfire, explicitly linking it to the Quranic concept of 'lahw al-hadith' (amusing discourse). This establishes a direct theological connection between musical entertainment and the spiritual danger of being led astray from the path of Allah, a view central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the permissibility of music. The Imam's recitation of the verse underscores that such discourse is not merely neutral entertainment but a tool for misguidance when it distracts from divine remembrance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Ismail, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, said, ‘I heard himasws saying, ‘The singing (music) is from what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Promised the Fire over it’, and heasws recited this Verse [31:6] And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from Allah’s Way without knowledge, and to take it for a mockery; these shall have an abasing Punishment’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn ’Isma‘il from ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:
“I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘music (and singing) is of such things for which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has warned with punishment in the fire.’

He (the Imam) then read this verse, ‘There are people who pay for worthless tales (or activities) that deviates them from the path of Allah without their realizing such bad results. They treat the signs of Allah with ridicule. It is such people who will suffer a humiliating torment.’ [31:6]”
